messages:
sam.r: Heads up 10: FinWave wants a 2-week Private deployment POC. Key asks: preserve source client IP for app-level auth, allow their TLS inspection in DMZ, and have an automatic fallback to a proxy if PrivateLink is blocked by their firewall. They asked for the simplest connectivity recommendation + minimal firewall ACLs and a note on potential cost impacts.

maria.s: Clarifying q: is the workload fully in their AWS account and will they host the inference nodes? Also need to know if they use TGW/transit for cross-account traffic.

sam.r: Yes, customer-managed VPC, we'll deploy our Private agent containers in their VPC. They have a TGW and an onprem DMZ where TLS inspection lives.

ben.n: Networking summary: two viable topologies that meet "preserve src IP": 1) VPC peering or TGW-based routed peering where no SNAT occurs between client and our pods. 2) PrivateLink with careful ENI routing and no NAT between the interface endpoint and pods (hard to guarantee if they add proxies).

ben.n: PrivateLink benefits: clear security boundary, per-endpoint quotas, simple DNS mapping. Drawback: interface endpoints appear behind ENIs and many teams route traffic via a proxy/NAT which will break src IP preservation.

olivia.k: For the TLS-inspect requirement, GET clarity: does their inspector reissue leaf certs? That will break any mutual TLS we attempt. If they reissue, we either need to trust their CA for inbound mTLS or move to a dedicated private deploy inside their subnet so there is no reissue between client and container.

kevin.t: Security must-haves to collect from them:
- TLS-inspect behavior (reissue Y/N)
- list of egress proxies and public IPs that will originate traffic
- VPC CIDR(s) and route table excerpts for subnets we'll use
- whether they will terminate with a managed NAT GW in front of interface endpoints

sam.r: They want a template SG/ACL they can paste. Can we provide a minimal set now?

ben.n: Minimal guidance (to paste into their customer SGs):
- If PrivateLink: Outbound TCP 443 to interface endpoint ENI IPs (replace with actual ENI IPs we share)
- If Peering/TGW: Allow inbound/outbound between VPC CIDRs on 443 and 10250 (K8s health checks)
- If proxy fallback: Allow outbound to proxy IPs on 443, and allow proxy -> endpoint/enclave IPs on 443

ben.n: Example SG rule (AWS console friendly) to allow PrivateLink egress:
```
Outbound rule:
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
Port range: 443
Destination: <REPLACE_WITH_INTERFACE_ENI_IPS>
Description: Allow traffic to Redwood Private interface endpoints
```

olivia.k: Also include DNS guidance: they should create a Route53 private hosted zone or endpoint-centric DNS override so our service DNS resolves to interface endpoint IPs. If they use split-horizon DNS, ensure the test pods resolve the private name.

maria.s: Cost note for SOW: PrivateLink may add per-endpoint hourly charges and per-GB processing charges in some regions. If traffic flows through their egress NAT/proxy, include potential NAT bandwidth charges. We'll add a short clause: "Customer responsible for any cloud provider data egress and PrivateLink endpoint charges."

kevin.t: Operational runbook items for POC:
- Customer provides sanitized network diagram + CIDRs + proxy IP list
- We provide an ENI IP list and DNS override entries to their infra team
- Customer applies SG/ACL with verbatim rules we supply
- Smoke tests: check src-IP preservation (curl -v to test endpoint, examine X-Forwarded-For / connection source), streaming stability, and artifact retrieval (S3 access)

sam.r: Who owns what?
- Maria/Ben: network runbook + SG/ACL templates (due: EOD tomorrow)
- Olivia: TLS/mTLS edge cases doc (due: EOD tomorrow)
- Kevin: security questionnaire answers + acceptance criteria (due: EOD tomorrow)
- Sam: compile SOW note on PrivateLink costs and schedule pre-POC call

deploy-bot: Note: Private control plane region options: us-east-1 or customer region. Plan canary in us-east-1 on 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC; expect 1-2 hour window.

maria.s: Add fallback pattern in runbook: PrivateLink primary, proxy fallback if inspect/NAT prevents src-IP preservation. Document how to detect (curl test shows proxy IP) and how to toggle proxy fallback in config.

ben.n: One more caveat: if they enforce TLS inspection that reissues certs and we rely on client certs for auth, recommend dedicated private deployment in-customer-subnet (no proxy) or shared trust of their CA and update our client auth rules.

sam.r: I'll ask the customer for the sanitized diagram today. Once we have it we'll pick PrivateLink-first or Peering-first and lock change control.

olivia.k: I'll prepare a short checklist to validate TLS inspect behavior during the POC call.

kevin.t: :white_check_mark:

sam.r: Thanks everyone. I'll post the diagram when I have it and schedule the pre-POC kickoff.
